passages.text: Although a spotted hyena is smaller than a lion, the bite force of a hyena is greater than ______ lion of comparable age, allowing it to crack bones that lions usually leave behind.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Coating tests
passages.text: In the laboratory, one group of engineers sprayed salt water on coated steel panels every hour for six weeks. ______ a second group placed identical panels on a pier by the ocean and checked them once a week for rust.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Fresco notes
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• A fifteenth-century fresco covers the walls of a small chapel in central Italy.
• Conservators began restoring it in 2009.
• They removed centuries of grime by hand, a few square centimeters at a time.
• The restoration was completed in 2021.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Bacteria experiment
passages.text: Because the samples had been contaminated during shipping ______ the team discarded them and repeated the entire experiment with fresh cultures.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Steps by season
passages.text:
A study measured the average number of steps taken per day by adults in three age groups during summer and winter.
Age group | Summer | Winter
20–39 | 8,200 | 7,600
40–59 | 7,500 | 6,700
60 and older | 6,400 | 4,800
The researchers claim that the drop in daily steps from summer to winter was largest for adults aged 60 and older.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: The rehearsal
passages.text:
The following text is from a short story.
The orchestra had rehearsed the symphony's final movement eleven times that week. On the twelfth run, the conductor lowered her baton halfway through, said nothing for a long moment, and then told the musicians to go home early. Several of them looked at one another, unsure whether they had played very badly or very well.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: A trial semester
passages.text: When the school board reviewed the proposal to keep the public library open until 9 p.m., its response was ______: members praised the plan's goals but voted to fund only a one-semester trial before committing to a permanent change.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Beaten thin
passages.text: Gold is unusually ______: a single gram of it can be hammered into a sheet nearly one square meter in area without tearing, a property that has made gold leaf a favorite of artists and bookbinders for centuries.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Worms that came later
passages.text: For much of the twentieth century, many gardeners and naturalists in the northern United States and Canada assumed that the earthworms in local forests had always lived there. Studies of species and their histories, however, indicate that most earthworms in these northern forests arrived from Europe and Asia in soil and plants carried by settlers, because the glaciers of the last ice age had largely wiped out native earthworms in the region. Ecologists now study how these newcomers alter the leaf litter and soil of forests that developed without them.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Narrow rings
passages.text: Researchers examining tree rings in a mountain valley found that pines on dry, south-facing slopes formed unusually narrow rings for an entire decade in the 1800s. Pines of the same species growing beside the valley's river, where groundwater is always available, formed rings of normal width during the same decade. These findings suggest that the narrow rings most likely reflect ______
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Three gardens
passages.text:
A city tracked three community gardens during one growing season.
Garden | Number of plots | Total harvest (kg)
A | 40 | 2,000
B | 25 | 1,500
C | 15 | 1,050
A city report claims that Garden C was the most productive per plot even though it had the fewest plots.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: A farmer's find
passages.text: The silver coins, ______ in 1903 by a farmer plowing a field near the river, are now displayed at the county museum alongside the farmer's own account of the discovery.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Three generations
passages.text: Marisol Vega's 2015 novel The Orchards ______ the story of three generations of a family who run a fruit farm in central California, moving back and forth among their perspectives.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: A fish without eyes
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Ozark cavefish is a small, pale fish with no functional eyes.
• It lives in caves and underground streams.
• Its range is limited to parts of Missouri, Arkansas, and Oklahoma.
• It is listed as threatened under the US Endangered Species Act.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Eleven prototypes
passages.text: Although her first designs failed every field test, the engineer remained ______, rebuilding and retesting the water filter eleven times over three years until it finally met the village council's standard.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Weighing two readings
passages.text: Reviewers praised the historian's account of the 1848 uprising as ______: it lays out the strengths of both rival interpretations of the event before cautiously favoring one of them.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Lights on the beach
passages.text: Newly hatched sea turtles find the ocean by heading toward the brightest part of the horizon, which on an undeveloped beach is usually the open sky above the water. Along developed coastlines, however, streetlights and lit windows can be brighter than the sea, and hatchlings may crawl inland, where many die. In response, a number of coastal towns now require residents to shield or turn off outdoor lights visible from the beach during nesting season.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Folding leaves
passages.text: Botanist Lena Ortiz hypothesizes that a desert shrub folds its leaves in the hottest part of the day mainly to reduce the amount of water the leaves lose.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: A quieter motor
passages.text: After two years of development, the appliance maker announced that ______ new electric motor for washing machines runs about 40 percent more quietly than the model it replaces.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: An old crossing
passages.text: The Fennick River ferry carried passengers and freight for nearly a century before the county built a bridge at the same crossing in 1931, ______ remains in daily use and was widened in 1978.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: A field without a plow
passages.text: For generations, farmers in the region prepared their fields each spring by plowing the soil deeply. ______ a growing number now plant directly into the stubble of the previous crop, a practice that leaves the soil undisturbed and helps it hold water.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Glass frogs
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Glass frogs live in the rainforests of Central and South America.
• Many have skin on their undersides so transparent that their hearts and other organs are visible.
• When glass frogs sleep, most of their red blood cells move into the liver.
• This makes the frogs about two to three times more transparent while they rest.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Listening plants
passages.text: Some plants appear to respond to the vibrations made by insects feeding on them. ______ in one experiment, thale cress plants that had been exposed to recorded vibrations of caterpillars chewing produced more of a defensive chemical when caterpillars later fed on them than plants that had not been exposed to such vibrations did.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Who has seen the wind?
passages.text: "Who Has Seen the Wind?" is an 1872 poem by Christina Rossetti. In the poem, the speaker suggests that the wind's presence can be known through its effects on the natural world.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Brief blooms
passages.text: Some desert wildflowers are strikingly ______: after a rare heavy rain they sprout, bloom, and drop their seeds within a few weeks, then disappear from the landscape until the next downpour, which may be years away.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: A cautious announcement
passages.text: In interviews about her team's discovery, the astronomer's tone was notably ______: she called the result "interesting" rather than "groundbreaking" and repeatedly stressed how much remained unknown.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Safety in numbers
passages.text: Periodical cicadas in parts of North America spend 13 or 17 years underground as nymphs and then emerge by the millions within a few weeks. This timing is not a coincidence. Birds and other predators can eat only a small fraction of such an enormous swarm, so most of the cicadas survive long enough to mate, a strategy biologists call predator satiation.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: A regular dip
passages.text: Astronomers observing a distant star found that its brightness dropped by the same small amount every 12.4 days, with each dip lasting about three hours. Random changes on a star's surface do not repeat on such a precise schedule. The astronomers therefore concluded that ______
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Litter by type
passages.text:
Volunteers counted the litter collected during an annual beach cleanup. The town banned single-use plastic bags in 2022.
Litter type | 2021 | 2023
Plastic bottles | 420 | 210
Cigarette butts | 650 | 600
Plastic bags | 300 | 90
A local report claims that, from 2021 to 2023, plastic bags showed the largest percentage decrease of any litter type in the table.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: One hand or two? (two texts)
passages.text:
Text 1
A historian argues that a fourteenth-century manuscript of sermons was copied entirely by a single scribe, citing the remarkably consistent shape of the letters from the first page to the last.

Text 2
Scribes trained in the same workshop were taught to imitate a single house style so closely that their hands can be hard to tell apart. In this manuscript, analysis of the parchment shows that the last third was made from animal skins prepared differently from those used in the first two-thirds.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Mountain pastures
passages.text: Each spring, the ______ of the valley drive their goats up to the high pastures, where the animals graze until the first snow.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Above all
passages.text: The expedition's success depended on one thing more than any other ______ the weather in the narrow window when the pass would be free of ice.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Inefficient but indispensable
passages.text: The earliest steam engines were enormously inefficient, turning only a tiny fraction of the energy in their fuel into useful work. ______ they transformed mining in eighteenth-century Britain, because they could pump water out of deep mines far faster than teams of horses could.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Refill stations
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In 2023, Ridgeview High School installed four water-bottle refill stations.
• Sales of bottled water in Ridgeview's cafeteria fell by 40 percent that year.
• Each station cost about $1,500 to install.
• The district's two other high schools have no refill stations.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: One shared style
passages.text: The proposed link between the two ancient settlements remains ______: it rests entirely on a single shared pottery style, which could just as easily have spread between unrelated communities through trade.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Slow gains
passages.text: Rather than arriving in a sudden breakthrough, the improvement in phone battery life over the past decade has been ______, with each new generation lasting only slightly longer than the one before it.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: A risky descent
passages.text: Three-toed sloths spend nearly all their lives in trees, yet about once a week they climb down to the ground to defecate, a trip that exposes them to predators. Researchers have found that moths living in sloth fur lay their eggs in the dung. The moths later return to the fur, where they appear to add nutrients that help algae grow there, and sloths sometimes eat that algae. Based on these findings, the researchers proposed that the risky descent ______
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Three wheat varieties
passages.text:
Researchers grew three varieties of wheat on 10 farms and recorded each variety's yield, in metric tons per hectare.
Variety | Average yield | Lowest yield | Highest yield
A | 4.1 | 3.8 | 4.4
B | 4.3 | 3.6 | 4.9
C | 4.6 | 2.9 | 6.0
The researchers claim that variety C produced the highest yields on average but was also the least consistent from farm to farm.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Composed on the spot? (two texts)
passages.text:
Text 1
A music critic describes jazz improvisation as composition in its purest form: a soloist invents an entirely new melody in the moment, with nothing prepared in advance.

Text 2
Studies of recorded jazz solos have found that experienced players frequently reuse short melodic phrases, often called licks, that they practiced beforehand. Skilled improvisers combine and vary these familiar phrases in new ways as they respond to the music around them.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: A first program
passages.text: Ada Lovelace, a mathematician by ______ wrote in 1843 a set of notes on a proposed calculating machine that included what many historians consider the first published computer program.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Sold out
passages.text: By noon the bakery had sold every loaf of bread ______ by evening, even the last tray of pastries was gone.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Trees and fire
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The cones of lodgepole pines are often sealed with resin that melts in the heat of a fire, releasing seeds onto the burned ground.
• Jack pines also have cones that open mainly after exposure to fire.
• Some eucalyptus trees sprout new shoots from buds under their bark after a fire.
• All three kinds of trees grow in places where wildfires occur regularly.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Prices without minutes
passages.text: No rule in the guild's charter forbade members from undercutting one another's prices, yet historians believe members observed a ______ understanding on the matter: the records of guild meetings never mention prices at all, but members' prices stayed within a few pennies of one another for decades.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: A small jaw
passages.text: The fossil's modest size ______ its significance: the jaw, barely two centimeters long, preserves a pattern of tooth replacement that researchers had predicted for fish of its age but had never before observed.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: A relay across generations
passages.text: Each fall, monarch butterflies from eastern North America fly thousands of kilometers to forests in central Mexico, where they spend the winter. In spring they head north, but no individual completes the return. The butterflies breed along the way, and it is their children and grandchildren that continue the journey and reach the northern United States and Canada. The monarchs that fly south again in the fall may therefore be the great-grandchildren of those that left Mexico in spring.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Urban coyotes
passages.text: Food from people, such as garbage and pet food, is plentiful in cities and takes little effort for coyotes to obtain, so one might expect urban coyotes that eat it to be healthier than coyotes that hunt. A 2015 study in Edmonton, Canada, found the reverse: coyotes whose diets included more human food were in poorer body condition and more likely to have mange. One possible explanation is that human food, though plentiful, is low in the protein that coyotes need, which would mean that ______
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Window treatments
passages.text:
Researchers recorded the average number of bird collisions per month at office buildings before and after one of three window treatments was installed.
Treatment | Before | After
Dot-pattern film | 20 | 6
UV-reflective glass | 40 | 22
Exterior netting | 10 | 4
The researchers concluded that, relative to each building group's starting level, the dot-pattern film was the most effective of the three treatments.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Following a point (two texts)
passages.text:
Text 1
In experiments where a person points to one of two cups hiding food, pet dogs choose the correct cup far more often than chimpanzees do. Some researchers have concluded that domestication gave dogs an inborn sensitivity to human gestures that their wild relatives lack.
Text 2
Other researchers have found that wolves raised by people from birth can follow pointing about as well as pet dogs, while shelter dogs with little human contact often struggle with the task. These researchers argue that a dog's experience with people shapes this skill more than has been recognized.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Twelve receptors
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Humans have three types of color photoreceptors.
• Mantis shrimp have twelve types of color photoreceptors.
• Researchers expected mantis shrimp to tell apart very similar colors.
• In a 2014 study, mantis shrimp could not reliably distinguish colors that people can easily tell apart.
• The researchers suggested that the shrimp may identify colors directly instead of comparing signals from different receptors.

passages.title: Otters and kelp
passages.text: Sea otters eat sea urchins, and where otters have returned to the coast, urchin numbers have dropped and kelp forests have regrown. ______ the otters' appetite for crabs and clams has brought them into conflict with people who harvest those animals for food.

passages.text: The Voynich manuscript, a fifteenth-century book written in an unknown ______ has resisted every attempt at decipherment, including efforts by professional codebreakers during the twentieth century.

passages.title: A contaminated plate
passages.text: In September 1928, Alexander Fleming returned from a vacation and found that a mold had contaminated one of the culture plates in his laboratory. He noticed that the mold growing on the plate ______ the bacteria immediately around it.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Draupner wave
passages.text: For decades, sailors' reports of "rogue waves" (single waves more than twice as tall as the surrounding seas) were often dismissed as exaggerations, since standard models predicted that such waves should be extremely rare. Then, on January 1, 1995, a laser sensor on the Draupner oil platform in the North Sea recorded a wave about 26 meters high amid seas of roughly 12 meters. Researchers have since revised their models, and satellite surveys suggest rogue waves are more common than once believed.

questions.evidence: ferns crowded every bench, and vines had climbed all the way to the cracked glass roof
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: teeming
choices.B: devoid
choices.C: reminiscent
choices.D: wary

questions.explanation: The colon introduces evidence that the greenhouse was full of plants. "Teeming with life" means crowded with living things, which matches ferns on every bench and vines up to the roof.

distractor_explanations.B: "Devoid" means completely lacking, the opposite of what the details describe.
distractor_explanations.C: "Reminiscent" means suggestive of something else and is followed by "of," not "with"; it does not describe abundance.
distractor_explanations.D: "Wary" means cautious, a quality of people or animals, not of a greenhouse.

hints: What do the details after the colon show about the greenhouse?
Predict a word meaning 'full of' before reading the choices.

strategy.explanation: Predict "full," then choose the closest precise word.

questions.remember: Let the text's evidence choose the word.

questions.evidence: "A long span on a weak foundation," he says, "is simply a dramatic way to fail."
questions.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the quotation in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It presents a counterargument that Reyes goes on to reject.
choices.B: It explains how engineers measure the span of a bridge.
choices.C: It illustrates, in memorable terms, why Reyes believes a bridge's foundation matters more than its span.
choices.D: It suggests that most existing bridges were built on weak foundations.

questions.explanation: Reyes claims the foundation is the most important part of a bridge. The quotation backs that claim with a vivid image: however impressive the span, a weak foundation means failure.

distractor_explanations.A: The quotation is Reyes's own statement supporting his view, not a counterargument.
distractor_explanations.B: The quotation says nothing about how spans are measured.
distractor_explanations.D: The quotation describes a hypothetical case and makes no claim about most existing bridges.

hints: What is Reyes's main claim?
How does the quotation relate to that claim?

strategy.explanation: Identify the claim first, then ask how the quotation serves it.

questions.remember: Function questions ask what a part does for the whole.

questions.evidence: Organizers say the event keeps hundreds of items out of the landfill each year. Just as important, they add, residents who watch the repairs often learn to fix similar problems on their own.
questions.stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: The repair café in Alder Creek mainly repairs bicycles.
choices.B: A monthly event in Alder Creek reduces waste and helps residents learn to fix things themselves.
choices.C: Volunteers in Alder Creek are paid to repair residents' household items.
choices.D: Residents of Alder Creek throw away fewer items than residents of other towns do.

questions.explanation: The text describes the repair café and its two benefits: keeping items out of the landfill and teaching residents repair skills. B captures both.

distractor_explanations.A: Bicycles are one example among several; the text does not say they are the main focus.
distractor_explanations.C: The repairs are done for free by volunteers; nothing says the volunteers are paid.
distractor_explanations.D: The text makes no comparison with other towns.

hints: What is the whole text about?
Which choice includes both benefits the organizers mention?

strategy.explanation: Summarize in one sentence, then match.

questions.remember: The main idea covers the whole text, not one example.

questions.evidence: 1 | Sunflower seeds | 212
questions.stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support the student's conclusion?

choices.A: Feeder 1, which held sunflower seeds, had 212 visits, more than either the thistle feeder (87) or the suet feeder (145).
choices.B: Feeder 2, which held thistle seeds, had 87 visits, fewer than Feeder 3.
choices.C: Together, the three feeders received 444 visits.
choices.D: Feeder 3, which held suet, had 145 visits.

questions.explanation: The conclusion is that sunflower seeds attracted the most visits. Supporting it requires comparing the sunflower feeder with both others: 212 is greater than 87 and 145. Only A makes that full comparison.

distractor_explanations.B: This compares only the other two feeders and says nothing about sunflower seeds.
distractor_explanations.C: The total does not show which food attracted the most visits.
distractor_explanations.D: One feeder's count alone cannot show which food was most popular.

hints: What exactly does the conclusion claim?
Which choice compares sunflower seeds with both other foods?

strategy.explanation: Restate the claim, then choose the data that compares all three.

questions.remember: A 'most' claim needs a comparison with every other option.

questions.evidence: within ten years, the number of businesses along its route had tripled.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.D: 1825, which

questions.explanation: "The town's first canal opened in 1825" and "within ten years, the number of businesses along its route had tripled" are both independent clauses. A semicolon correctly joins two independent clauses.

distractor_explanations.A: A comma alone between two independent clauses creates a comma splice.
distractor_explanations.C: With no punctuation, the two independent clauses run together.
distractor_explanations.D: "Which" makes the second part a relative clause, but the rest of the sentence ("within ten years, the number … had tripled") cannot follow "which" grammatically.

hints: Is each part of the sentence a complete sentence on its own?
What punctuation can join two complete sentences without a conjunction?

strategy.explanation: Two independent clauses with no conjunction need a semicolon or a period.

questions.remember: Semicolon: two complete sentences, no conjunction.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.B: have offered
choices.C: offers
choices.D: are offering

questions.evidence: Most frogs lay their eggs in water, where the young hatch as swimming tadpoles.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: for example,
choices.B: therefore,
choices.C: however,
choices.D: similarly,

questions.explanation: The first sentence describes most frogs; the second describes coquí frogs doing the opposite (eggs on land, no tadpoles). "However" signals that contrast.

distractor_explanations.A: Coquí frogs are an exception to the pattern, not an example of it.
distractor_explanations.B: The coquí's behavior is not a result of what most frogs do.
distractor_explanations.D: "Similarly" signals likeness, but the coquí differs from most frogs.

hints: Is the coquí like most frogs or different from them?
Choose the transition that signals that relationship.

strategy.explanation: Predict a contrast word such as 'but,' then match.

questions.remember: Name the relationship before choosing the transition.

questions.evidence: Glass can be recycled again and again without losing quality.
questions.stem: The student wants to emphasize a difference between recycling glass and recycling plastic. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Glass bottles and plastic bottles can both be recycled.
choices.B: Recycled glass is often used to make new bottles.
choices.C: Both glass and plastic are commonly used to make bottles, and both can be recycled.
choices.D: Glass can be recycled again and again without losing quality, whereas most plastics can be recycled only a few times before the material degrades.

questions.explanation: The goal is a difference. D contrasts how many times each material can be recycled, using "whereas" to make the difference explicit.

distractor_explanations.A: This states a similarity, not a difference.
distractor_explanations.B: This gives information about glass only, with no comparison to plastic.
distractor_explanations.C: This states similarities between the materials.

hints: The goal is to emphasize a difference.
Which choice mentions both materials and contrasts them?

strategy.explanation: Underline the goal (difference), then eliminate choices that state similarities or mention one material.

questions.remember: Synthesis questions: the stated goal decides the answer.

questions.evidence: Yet when researchers measured trehalose in several tardigrade species, they found little or none.
questions.stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.A: It presents two competing explanations and concludes that neither is supported.
choices.B: It describes an experiment and then lists that experiment's limitations.
choices.C: It describes a long-held assumption, presents evidence against it, and then reports an alternative explanation.
choices.D: It introduces an animal and compares it with other organisms that produce trehalose.

questions.explanation: The text opens with an assumption (trehalose protects tardigrades), gives evidence against it (little or no trehalose found), and ends with an alternative (tardigrade-specific proteins forming a gel).

distractor_explanations.A: The text does reach a supported explanation: the proteins.
distractor_explanations.B: No limitations of an experiment are listed.
distractor_explanations.D: The text mentions other organisms only briefly and does not compare tardigrades with them.

hints: Track the text sentence by sentence: assumption, then what?
What does the last sentence offer?

strategy.explanation: Label each sentence's role, then match the sequence.

questions.remember: Structure questions: label each sentence's job.

questions.evidence: describes a neglected orchard as both decaying and still productive
questions.stem: Which quotation from "The Old Orchard" most effectively illustrates the claim?

choices.A: "Wind has stripped the orchard to its bones."
choices.B: "Each autumn the pickers fill their baskets."
choices.C: "The farmhouse windows glow at dusk."
choices.D: "The branches sag with rot, and still they bloom."

questions.explanation: The claim has two parts: decaying and still productive. "The branches sag with rot" shows decay, and "still they bloom" shows continued growth. Only D shows both.

distractor_explanations.A: This shows decay only.
distractor_explanations.B: This shows productivity only, and it describes the pickers, not the orchard's condition.
distractor_explanations.C: This describes the farmhouse, not the orchard.

hints: The claim has two parts. What are they?
Which quotation shows both at once?

strategy.explanation: Eliminate quotations that show only one half of the claim.

questions.remember: Two-part claims need evidence for both parts.

questions.evidence: the folding ladder, the safety pin, and the paper clip
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: forgotten:
choices.B: forgotten;
choices.C: forgotten, which
choices.D: forgotten and

questions.explanation: The first part is a complete sentence that announces three objects, and the list that follows names them. A colon correctly introduces a list after a complete clause.

distractor_explanations.B: A semicolon must join two independent clauses, but the list is not a clause.
distractor_explanations.C: "Which" cannot introduce a list of nouns without a verb.
distractor_explanations.D: "And" joins the list to the clause ungrammatically, leaving no verb for the list.

hints: Is the part before the blank a complete sentence?
What punctuation introduces a list that explains what came before?

strategy.explanation: A complete clause followed by a list calls for a colon.

questions.remember: Use a colon after a complete clause to introduce a list.

choices.A: were

choices.C: was

distractor_explanations.A: "Were" agrees with "volunteers" or "booths," not the true subject "Each."
distractor_explanations.B: "Have been" is plural.

Is "each" singular or plural?

questions.evidence: they had measured the lake's temperature at different depths
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: scientist's
choices.B: scientists
choices.C: scientists's
choices.D: scientists'

questions.explanation: The findings belong to two scientists, so the plural possessive is needed. For a plural noun ending in s, add only an apostrophe: "scientists'."

distractor_explanations.A: "Scientist's" is singular possessive, but there are two scientists.
distractor_explanations.B: "Scientists" without an apostrophe is a plain plural, not a possessive.
distractor_explanations.C: "Scientists's" is not standard for a plural possessive.

hints: How many scientists are there?
How is a plural noun ending in s made possessive?

strategy.explanation: Plural + possessive = s'.

questions.remember: Plural possessive: add just an apostrophe after s.

questions.evidence: Some critics predicted that the redesigned riverside park would attract few visitors.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Similarly,
choices.B: Therefore,
choices.C: On the contrary,
choices.D: For example,

questions.explanation: The critics predicted few visitors; attendance instead doubled. "On the contrary" signals that the second sentence contradicts the prediction.

distractor_explanations.A: "Similarly" signals agreement, but doubled attendance contradicts the prediction.
distractor_explanations.B: "Therefore" signals a result, but the prediction did not cause the attendance.
distractor_explanations.D: Doubled attendance is not an example of the critics' prediction.

hints: Did the attendance match or contradict the prediction?
Pick the transition for that relationship.

strategy.explanation: Predict 'but actually,' then match.

questions.remember: Name the relationship, then the transition.

questions.evidence: Her 1962 mural Morning Platform is her best-known work.
questions.stem: The student wants to introduce Lin Adeyemi and her best-known work to an audience unfamiliar with her. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Lin Adeyemi, a twentieth-century painter known for her murals of ordinary commuters in train stations, is best remembered for her 1962 mural Morning Platform.
choices.B: Morning Platform is Lin Adeyemi's best-known mural.
choices.C: Ordinary commuters appear in many murals painted in train stations.
choices.D: In 1962, a mural called Morning Platform was painted.

questions.explanation: An unfamiliar audience needs to know who Adeyemi was as well as her best-known work. A identifies her as a twentieth-century muralist of commuters and names Morning Platform.

distractor_explanations.B: This names the work but does not tell an unfamiliar audience who Adeyemi was.
distractor_explanations.C: This does not mention Adeyemi or her work.
distractor_explanations.D: This omits the painter entirely.

hints: What does an audience unfamiliar with her need to know first?
Which choice covers both the painter and the work?

strategy.explanation: The goal has two parts: introduce her and her best-known work.

questions.remember: Introductions identify the subject before details.

questions.evidence: definitions memorized for a quiz are often forgotten within weeks
questions.stem: Based on the texts, how would the researchers in Text 2 most likely respond to the claim in Text 1?

choices.A: They would argue that quizzes are the most reliable way to measure vocabulary growth.
choices.B: They would grant that memorizing lists can raise quiz scores quickly but question whether those gains last.
choices.C: They would claim that students cannot learn any new words by memorizing lists.
choices.D: They would suggest that reading builds vocabulary faster than memorizing lists does.

questions.explanation: Text 1 claims lists are the fastest way to build vocabulary, citing quick quiz gains. Text 2 does not deny quick gains; it says memorized definitions are often forgotten within weeks, while words met in reading tend to stick. So the researchers would accept the short-term gains but doubt they last.

distractor_explanations.A: Text 2 implies quiz results can mislead, since memorized words fade; it does not call quizzes the most reliable measure.
distractor_explanations.C: Text 2 says memorized words are "often forgotten," not that students learn none; "cannot learn any" goes too far.
distractor_explanations.D: Text 2 argues that reading leads to better retention, not faster learning.

hints: Does Text 2 deny that lists raise quiz scores?
What does Text 2 say happens weeks later?

strategy.explanation: Find where Text 2 addresses memorized definitions, then pick the response that matches its partial agreement.

questions.remember: Watch for partial agreement and extreme wording.

questions.evidence: When the largest crab moves into the new shell, the next crab in line takes the shell it left behind, and so on down the line.
questions.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: hermit crabs generally prefer shells that are too small for them.
choices.B: only the largest crab in the group ends up with a better-fitting shell.
choices.C: hermit crabs line up beside a new shell without regard to their size.
choices.D: a single new shell can lead to several crabs in the group moving into larger shells.

questions.explanation: Each crab that moves leaves its old shell for the next crab, and the chain continues down the line. So one new shell lets many crabs upgrade, not just one.

distractor_explanations.A: The crabs move into larger shells, which suggests they seek a better fit, not smaller shells.
distractor_explanations.B: The chain of moves means crabs after the largest one also get larger shells.
distractor_explanations.C: The text says the crabs line up by size.

hints: Follow the chain: what happens to each shell that is left behind?
How many crabs end up in a new shell?

strategy.explanation: Trace the sequence in the second sentence to its result.

questions.remember: Completion questions follow the text's logic to its next step.

questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: strident

questions.remember: To weaken a claim, find a result it predicts wrongly.

questions.evidence: Unlike foam packaging, mycelium packaging breaks down in soil within a few weeks.
questions.stem: The student wants to emphasize an environmental advantage of mycelium packaging over foam packaging. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.B: Unlike foam, packaging grown from mycelium, the root-like network of a fungus, breaks down in soil within weeks.
choices.C: Though it is grown from a fungus, mycelium packaging currently costs more to produce than foam packaging.

questions.evidence: long before humans took any deliberate role in their breeding
questions.stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the argument made by "some researchers" in the text?

choices.A: Remains from the earliest farming villages show that people confined and selectively bred cats from the start.

choices.C: Wild cats in some regions still scavenge for food near human settlements today.
choices.D: The genetic differences between domestic and wild cats accumulated over many millennia.

strategy.explanation: For each finding, ask whether it fits or conflicts with self-domestication.

questions.subskill: Sentence boundaries with a subordinate clause
questions.evidence: a safety concern emerged in the final month
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: early. Although
choices.B: early, although
choices.C: early; although,
choices.D: early although

questions.explanation: "Although the results had looked promising" is a subordinate clause attached to the main clause "a safety concern emerged." That full sentence must be separated from "The trial ... was halted early," which is also complete: a period does it.

distractor_explanations.B: This joins "The trial ... was halted early" to a second independent clause ("a safety concern emerged") with only a comma, a comma splice.
distractor_explanations.C: A comma should not follow "although," which introduces a clause.
distractor_explanations.D: The two independent clauses run together without punctuation.

hints: Which clause does "although ..." belong to?
How many independent clauses are there?

strategy.explanation: Find each subject-verb pair that can stand alone, then check the boundary.

questions.remember: An "although" clause attaches to the clause after it, not before.

questions.evidence: fertilizer increased yield only when water was plentiful
questions.stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support the researchers' conclusion?

questions.evidence: relative to each building group's starting level
questions.stem: Which choice best describes data from the table that support the researchers' conclusion?

choices.A: Collisions fell by 18 per month with UV-reflective glass, the largest drop of the three.
choices.B: Netting cut collisions by 60%, from 10 to 4 per month, the lowest final count of the three.
choices.C: Dot film buildings ended at 6 collisions per month, less than a third of the UV glass buildings' 22.
choices.D: Collisions fell by 70% with dot-pattern film, 45% with UV glass, and 60% with netting.

questions.explanation: Relative reductions: dot film (20-6)/20 = 70%, UV glass (40-22)/40 = 45%, netting (10-4)/10 = 60%. The dot film's 70% is the largest, supporting the conclusion.

distractor_explanations.A: This is the largest drop in number, but the conclusion is about change relative to each starting level, and it favors UV glass.
distractor_explanations.B: This is true, but 60% is smaller than the dot film's 70%, so it does not show the dot film was most effective.
distractor_explanations.C: Comparing final counts ignores the different starting levels, which the conclusion explicitly accounts for.

hints: Is the conclusion about the size of the drop or the percentage?

strategy.explanation: Compute each percent decrease.

questions.remember: "Relative to the starting level" means percent change, not raw change.

strategy.explanation: Read the goal first, then look for the choice that pairs expectation with result.

questions.evidence: recorded a wave about 26 meters high amid seas of roughly 12 meters
questions.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the second sentence in the overall structure of the text?

choices.A: It offers an example of the kind of exaggerated report that the models were designed to explain.
choices.B: It explains how researchers revised their models so that they could predict the Draupner wave.
choices.C: It provides evidence that rogue waves are more common today than they were in earlier decades.
choices.D: It reports a direct observation that was difficult to reconcile with the models mentioned earlier.

questions.explanation: The first sentence says models predicted rogue waves (over twice the surrounding sea height) to be extremely rare; the second reports an instrument measuring a 26-meter wave amid 12-meter seas, a direct observation at odds with those models.

distractor_explanations.A: The 1995 record was an instrument measurement, not a sailor's exaggeration, and it contradicted the models.
distractor_explanations.B: The revision is mentioned only in the third sentence, as a later consequence.
distractor_explanations.C: The text says rogue waves are more common than once believed, not that they have become more frequent.

hints: Is the 1995 wave a sailor's report or a measurement?

strategy.explanation: Describe what the sentence does relative to the first sentence.

questions.remember: A function question asks what a sentence does, not just what it says.
